title: Herb Scissors Maintenance Checklist for Long‑Term Use
meta_description: Keep your shears sharp and clean. Follow our comprehensive herb scissors maintenance checklist to extend the life of your multi-blade kitchen tools.
html:
If you've ever tried to chop a bunch of cilantro or chives with a standard chef's knife, you know it takes time and a steady hand to get those tiny, uniform pieces. That is why multi-blade shears are a game-changer. However, because these tools have multiple points of contact and tight gaps between blades, they require a bit more care than your average kitchen scissors.

To keep your tools cutting smoothly, you need a consistent herb scissors maintenance checklist. When debris builds up between the blades, the shearing action weakens, and you end up bruising your herbs instead of slicing them. Here is how to ensure your shears last for years.

Immediate Post-Use Cleaning

The biggest enemy of multi-blade shears is organic buildup. Fresh herbs like basil and parsley release oils and moisture that, when combined with tiny leaf fragments, create a sticky residue. If this dries, it acts like glue, making the blades sluggish.

Always rinse your shears under warm running water immediately after use. If you are using the Herb Scissors, make full use of the included cleaning comb. The comb is designed to slide between the five blades, knocking loose the stubborn bits of greenery that a simple rinse might miss. This prevents the "clumping" effect that often happens in the center blades.

Deep Cleaning and Sanitization

While a quick rinse works for daily use, a weekly deep clean is necessary to prevent bacterial growth and mineral buildup. Avoid throwing your shears in the dishwasher. The high heat and harsh detergents can dull the blade edges and degrade the pivot screw over time.

Instead, use a soft brush or an old toothbrush dipped in mild dish soap. Scrub the pivot point—where the blades connect—as this is where grime tends to accumulate. After scrubbing, dry the blades immediately with a lint-free cloth. Leaving them to air dry can lead to water spots or, in some cases, small rust spots if the steel isn't fully stainless.

The Herb Scissors Maintenance Checklist for Blade Longevity

To make things easy, follow this periodic schedule to keep your equipment in top shape. Consistency is the difference between shears that last six months and shears that last a decade.

  • After every use: Rinse with warm water and use the cleaning comb to clear debris.
  • Daily: Hand dry completely to prevent oxidation.
  • Weekly: Scrub the pivot joint with a brush and soap; inspect for any loose screws.
  • Monthly: Apply a tiny drop of food-grade mineral oil to the pivot point to ensure smooth movement.
  • Seasonally: Check the blade alignment; if they are not meeting flush, gently tighten the center screw.

Sharpening and Edge Care

Because multi-blade shears have five separate cutting edges, sharpening them is more complex than sharpening a single knife. You cannot easily use a traditional whetstone without risking the alignment of the blades.

The best way to maintain the edge is through prevention. Only use your shears on soft herbs and small greens. Avoid cutting through thick stems, frozen herbs, or anything hard like nuts or plastic packaging. If you notice the blades are starting to "chew" the herbs rather than slicing them, you can use a fine-grit diamond hone or a professional sharpening service. For most home cooks, keeping the blades clean and oil-free is enough to maintain a sharp edge for a very long time.

Proper Storage Solutions

How you store your shears affects how often you'll need to perform maintenance. Tossing them into a crowded utensil drawer where they rub against other metal tools can cause microscopic nicks in the blades.

Store your shears in a dedicated slot or hang them if they have a hanging loop. If you keep them in a drawer, consider a protective sheath or a simple cloth wrap. This keeps the blades protected from impact and prevents dust from settling into the pivot mechanism, ensuring that the next time you reach for your Herb Scissors, they are ready to mince with precision.

FAQ

Can I put my herb scissors in the dishwasher?

It is highly recommended that you avoid the dishwasher. The intense heat and caustic chemicals can strip the finish and dull the precision edges of the five blades, leading to a shorter lifespan for the tool.

What is the best oil to use on the pivot screw?

Always use food-grade mineral oil. It is tasteless, odorless, and safe for use around food. Avoid using vegetable or olive oils, as these can go rancid over time and create a sticky residue that actually hinders the movement of the blades.

Why are my shears not cutting all the way through the herbs?

This is usually caused by one of two things: buildup of debris between the blades or a loose pivot screw. First, use the cleaning comb to ensure no residue is blocking the blades. If that doesn't work, check the center screw; if it's loose, the blades won't meet with enough pressure to slice cleanly.
